source.target: Source sync transactions, truncate replay, consumer publication, and existing adapter acknowledgements

preservation: Publish atomic coherent updates; do not expose intermediate graph states that are invalid as public results.
Subscribers receive changes that keep their promised view current.
Avoid a new adapter API. Interface spelling and behavioral compatibility must be distinguished.
Applied receipt means transaction writes and events became visible; successful exact subset load awaits its establishing receipts.
Accepted transactions apply in commit order; a later load rejection does not withdraw them.
Full snapshot transaction carries every synced row; partial subset transactions cannot make that declaration.
Materialized query replay retains its complete prior result through failure; initial/progressive loads are not all replacements.
Optimistic causal queue, persistence acceptance/durability and sync-run/ownership cancellation boundaries remain distinct.

Every source Collection read and every raw subscriber must retain the old snapshot through all replay load promise settlements, including failure. This is the strong draft oracle interpretation, not a conclusion of this extraction.
Completeness applies only to the declared scope; a promise settlement is not provider exhaustion or global source authority.

consumer replay barrier and private row buffer
actual result application precedes load fulfillment
replay scope and coherent current-input graph result; source-to-result boundaries
mutex, durable step and outward receipt distinction
canonical terms and many-to-many ownership/work/publication graph

primitives: Sync transaction and its acceptance/application obligation
Removal loses FIFO/no-withdrawal and coherent-batch reconstruction.
Exact acquisition and its response, receipt dependencies and final outcome
Removal loses cycle and distinction between response completeness and load settlement.
Public view with declared scope, rows and subscriber fold

Replacement authority over current owned demand

activeOverlaps: M1×M2: applied receipt links visible source changes to successful load settlement
M1×M3: source state, indexes, subscriber notification and receipt form one ordered application boundary
M2×M4: exact current-demand outcomes authorize a larger replacement; ownership change alters its membership
M3×M4: each consumer's declared complete result is withheld until its required work is authoritative
M1×M4: wrapper durability, optimistic causal holds and sync-run lifetime constrain application; not independent queue details
rules: Accept precedes application; application exposes transaction state/events before applied receipt; successful exact load follows receipts.
A successful load establishes only its exact demand; a full snapshot explicitly declares every row.
A materialized query may advance private graph input while its public result remains held.
Failed authoritative replay and obsolete/aborted work cannot certify current materialized replacement.
Changing the boundary can preserve API spelling while changing the semantic contract. Such loss must be named.

Precommit buffering can combine known complete responses using existing transaction calls, only if the producer knows the full replacement scope and completion; core cannot invent this premise from partial commits.
conflicts: P9 reverses R1 when the load awaits its visibility receipt. Preserving both creates a wait cycle.
P2 says keep subscribers current, but source-commit visibility and retained whole-replacement view have different scopes. Must declare which public view each subscriber represents.
Provider response completeness need not equal successful load settlement, nor prove global source replacement; no implicit priority.
reconstruction: M1 application -> M3 source state/index; source notifications; receipt -> M2 load success
M1 source application advances direct view; O4 retains subscriber/query view until M4 current-demand verdict
Move application behind M4 verdict while O1 still places verdict behind receipt: dependency cycle
Wrapper mutex can cover core application wait and durable work; outward receipt needs durable and visible; optimistic exception is retained as an extra premise
M4 scopes verdict to current ownership and sync/replay identity; accepted M1 transactions remain obligations
ablation: retained: removing it admits receipt fulfillment without visible writes and withdrawal of accepted writes
retained: removing it merges provider response and successful load settlement, hiding cycle
retained: removing it conflates source transaction atomicity with complete query publication
retained: removing it certifies replay from one fragment or obsolete acquisition
demoted to representation: no separate primitive needed
excluded: source semantics require dependencies, not current queue layout
not admitted: a possible implementation, not a primitive established by source
not admitted: proposal to vary, not part of frozen source
model.boundary: One source Collection, one unfiltered raw subscriber, one retained materialized result, one/two pre-enrolled demands, one transaction per response; owned-demand changes, mutex, optimism and native host remain source constraints outside executable abstraction.
model.range: No held-out marginal case supplied. Query and persisted witnesses were used for extraction and cannot count as independent range evidence.
model.negative: An applied receipt with the old public source rows/events, or a partial demand masquerading as a full snapshot, must be rejected.

forms.name: Publish source transactions; retain complete query results
forms.route: split existing source and derived-result publication scopes
forms.changes: Raw source subscriber folds follow each source commit; query publication retains its separate replay/window barrier.
preserves: P1 at a valid committed batch/current-input graph scope
P2 for source reads and raw source subscribers
losses: Revises established direct-subscriber replay buffering behavior.
Does not retain the prior complete source replacement through replay failure (P9).
Does not establish that arbitrary user projections cannot throw on partial source inputs.
forms.newStructure: Explicit distinction between source-batch consumers and complete materialized-result consumers; not a new adapter callback.
forms.coordination: All source read/index/event paths must share application; complete graph publication stays separate.
forms.boundary: Needs a product choice about direct source subscription replay behavior. Not a drop-in fix for the stronger draft oracle.

forms.name: Buffer known complete responses before an existing sync transaction
forms.route: rule combination: response completion + one existing atomic transaction + applied settlement
forms.changes: Producer gathers its declared complete replacement before begin/truncate/write/commit; demands then await that existing shared applied receipt.
preserves: P1 for declared source replacement scope under the complete-cohort premise
losses: Requires producer knowledge of complete replacement scope; ordinary partial commits do not provide it.
Buffer/coordination costs move earlier; bundled adapter implementations may change.
Publication precedes load-promise fulfillment, so it fails strict promise-timing P9 even for complete valid data.
A rejection after an accepted visible commit cannot restore Old without revising P5.
forms.newStructure: Precommit producer coordination, using one existing transaction rather than a new core staging callback.
forms.coordination: Unknown dynamic demand membership or independent adapters cannot be assumed coordinated. Full snapshot semantics require actual full-source authority.
forms.boundary: TLA passing cases assume fixed known cohort and before-commit failures; after-commit failure still has complete rows but violates failed-source-retention law.

exclusions.design: Resolve existing receipt while source stays private
exclusions.result: Rejected by current ReceiptVisibility contract; same signatures still change semantic API.

exclusions.design: Hold ordinary applied receipts until their loads succeed
exclusions.result: Circular wait in fixed-cohort model; accepted commits remain pending with no enabled Next application action.

exclusions.design: Treat one subset result or an empty source as complete global replacement
exclusions.result: Rejected by exact-scope/snapshot law; no provider exhaustion or coverage inferred.

process.status: FROZEN v3: source extraction, reconstruction, per-component ablation, 20 TLC configurations, exclusion, two adjacent forms and layer reconstruction complete. Independent range untested. Primary brief has not yet been drafted.
losses: Decomposition represents coherent rows abstractly and does not execute arbitrary user projections, include discovery, optimistic snapshots, dynamic peer enrollment, callback reentry or storage recovery.

encodingCorrections.reason: Make the stronger draft timing promise and stranded accepted commits explicit; v1 only tested complete source replacement versus progressive source, leaving strict pre-load visibility implicit.
Source-reader check found application over-approximation: encode FIFO using acceptedOrder; clarify one-coalesced-transaction abstraction, pre/postcommit failure bounds, and Spec stuttering.
encodingCorrections.effect: Corrected encoding and labels; no product law or invariant relaxed.

modelCheck.limits: TLC explores only the encoded finite grammar; no arbitrary projection validation, dynamic membership, abort, optimism, durability, reentry or eventual-response guarantee. Current split-view failure is reconstructed in Init, not generated by a truncate transition.

Two generated no-new-callback forms, each with consequential limits.
